beats: Hook (p25, 71:08-71:36): the favourite quantum code wants each check qubit wired to four data qubits; a heavy-hex chip offers at most three. Throw the code away, or compile around the gap? (line_qc_stitch_plug_socket). Cast as in QC03-01: the planner = the compiler, the fabricator = the chip maker; the quilt from QC03-04 = the surface code (patches = data qubits, knots = check qubits); a frame of hexagon bars = the heavy-hex chip.

The mismatch (p25): a square-grid code on a hexagon-lattice chip (line_qc_stitch_square_on_hex). p25's company logos are covered; never use 71:36-72:06 (a private conversation with a named researcher).

Two answers (72:06-72:31): hand-design a new code for every layout (line_qc_stitch_hand_made; e.g. IBM's heavy-hex code, Chamberland et al., PRX 2020), or let a compiler bridge the gap: Surf-Stitch (Wu, ..., Ding, ISCA 2022; tape p26), the first automated framework for compiling the surface code onto sparse chips.

Why it can be done (p26, 73:07-74:24; clip 73:07-73:33): error correction is like an approximate algorithm plus redundancy, so a check can be split: two helper qubits each gather the parity of two data qubits and then combine; one degree-4 node becomes two degree-3 nodes (line_qc_stitch_knot_split; reuse line_qc_surf_quilt_knots for the whole quilt).

The catch (74:24-74:51): every helper qubit is another place an error can start and spread into the data, so use as few as possible while keeping the code fault-tolerant (line_qc_stitch_snag); and there are many ways to split, a huge space to search.

Results (tape p27, 75:03-76:20): error thresholds on heavy-square and heavy-hex layouts, matching the expert design on one and beating it on the hardest; numbers only from the paper via FACTS.md (reuse line_balance).
Humans abstract, computers explore (clip 76:20-76:50): the person sets the rule, the compiler searches the many stitchings (line_qc_stitch_sewing_machine).

A logical grid on top of a physical graph (76:50-77:16), and the classical mindset helps derive the structure (clip 77:16-77:45) (line_qc_stitch_quilt_on_frame). Next (p28): code design and mapping as compiler problems; the theory under the codes is QC08.
Cover (line_qc_cover_03_05; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the planner sews a square quilt onto a frame of hexagon bars.
